title: dark-web-monitor-lite: A defensive Tor-aware keyword-watchlist monitor with rules-only matcher precision/recall measurement and a thorough compliance baseline
description: A small Python tool for defensive cyber-threat-intelligence (CTI) teams that watches a configurable list of publicly-known onion-service URLs for matches against a target watchlist of fictitious-by-default keywords, then dispatches alerts via Slack, Discord, or generic webhook. The tool is intentionally Tor-aware via the stem and httpx-socks libraries but degrades gracefully when no Tor SOCKS proxy is reachable: every fetcher returns a typed FetchResult (ok, http_error, network_error, tor_unavailable, timeout) so an operator can see coverage gaps in the report itself. Real measurements are reported on the matcher engine only — a labelled keyword corpus of 60 entries gives reproducible offline precision/recall/F1 for both exact and rapidfuzz fuzzy modes. Live onion fetches are deliberately not in the eval. The repository ships an unusually thorough compliance baseline: a deployment policy template, a four-jurisdiction (US, UK, EU, Pakistan) legal review, and an extensive ETHICAL_USE statement.
